title: Hotfix: revert aggressive mixed-workload batching default (p99 regression)
author: Sofia Ivanova
description:
Context: During Hosted canary rollout of the profile pack defaults on H100, we observed elevated tail latency (p99) on a mixed workload (short prefill + long decode) shortly after enabling the new batching defaults. Impact was isolated to the canary cohort but customer-visible for a subset of routes (see Incident references below).

Root cause (current understanding): The new default for mixed-workload batching increased effective queueing for long-decode requests when interleaved with bursty prefill traffic. Throughput was slightly better, but p99 increased 18–25% for the mixed bucket at concurrency >= 16. The perf-canary signal was present but did not block because the gate is currently warn-only for this bucket.

Change: Revert the overly aggressive batching default back to the previous safe values on the runtime-1.22 release branch. This restores prior p99 behavior while we rework the scheduler heuristics and gating thresholds.

What this PR does: (1) Reverts the default values for mixed-workload batching knobs (prefill coalescing window + max prefill tokens per batch) to pre-canary levels. (2) Leaves the new behavior available behind an explicit opt-in flag for internal experimentation. (3) Adds an extra startup log line to make the effective batching defaults obvious during on-call triage.

Incident references: Slack #incidents thread 1768901144 ("elevated tail latency after profile tweak") and #postmortems follow-ups 1768923300. Customer escalation: SUP-21941 (Dedicated H100 customer reporting higher p99 after upgrade; correlates with the same mixed bucket behavior).

Validation: Re-ran benchmark-lab mixed bucket on H100 (short prompt / long decode distribution) and compared against the canary build from Feb 6. p99 returned to within +2% of baseline while throughput stayed within -3% (acceptable for hotfix).

Rollout plan: Merge to release/runtime-1.22, deploy to Hosted canary immediately, expand to 25% after 2 hours if p99/p95 gates hold. Dedicated remains opt-in; SRE will notify on-call when canary looks healthy.

Follow-ups: (a) tighten perf-canary gate for mixed bucket p99 deltas, (b) revisit the heuristic with workload-bucket awareness rather than a global default, (c) update expected-behavior docs to call out trade-off explicitly.
commits: Revert "scheduler: increase mixed workload prefill batch ceiling"
runtime/scheduler: restore conservative defaults for mixed bucket
runtime/logging: print effective batching knobs at startup
tests: adjust golden config snapshot for release/runtime-1.22
conversation:
Sean Gallagher (SRE): Can we be explicit in the PR about which metrics drove the rollback and what the rollback trigger was? Also, please confirm kill-switch behavior is unchanged.

Sofia Ivanova (author): Added details to description + linked the Slack incident thread. Kill-switch is unchanged; this hotfix only changes the default knob values and adds an opt-in flag.

Marcus Reed: Do we have benchmark-lab numbers attached somewhere? I’m ok with reverting, but want to ensure we don’t silently accept a throughput hit.

Sofia Ivanova: Added a short summary in Validation. Full run is in benchmark-lab run 2026-02-06T23:41Z tagged profile_pack=1.0.0-rc3, commit=9f2c3c1 (internal link in the incident thread).

Noah Patel: Please ensure the opt-in flag name is consistent with other scheduler flags and that it’s wired through to the runtime config in Dedicated/Private.

Sofia Ivanova: Renamed to runtime.scheduler.aggressive_mixed_batching and added it to the config reference. Dedicated/Private wiring is via the existing runtime_flags.yaml ingestion (no control-plane changes needed).

Allison Grant: With the startup log line, can we include the active workload bucket thresholds too? Helps debugging when bucket classification changes.

Sofia Ivanova: For the hotfix I kept the log minimal (to avoid noisy logs / potential PII concerns). I opened ENG follow-up to add a debug endpoint field instead of logs.

Approvals: Sean Gallagher approved (after checklist + incident links). Marcus Reed approved. Noah Patel approved with minor nits addressed.
release_notes:
- Hotfix: revert mixed-workload batching defaults that increased p99 latency under interleaved prefill/decode traffic.
- Adds opt-in flag runtime.scheduler.aggressive_mixed_batching for controlled experimentation.
- Improves startup logging to surface effective batching knob values during on-call triage.
